case.subject: Leak sensor alert in vacant unit at Fernbrook Commons
case.body:
Hello Northgate Support,

I hope you are having a pleasant Saturday evening. I am writing because a little after 10:00 PM tonight I received a leak sensor alert from one of our vacant units here at Fernbrook Commons, and unfortunately there is no one on site who can go and check it right now. I am the community manager, but I am not on the property this evening, and our maintenance technician is off until Monday, so I have no way of knowing at the moment whether there is actually water running or whether the sensor has simply malfunctioned. The unit has been empty for a couple of weeks while we wait on a new resident, so nobody has been inside to notice anything, and I am concerned that if it is a real leak it could continue for hours and affect the units below it before anyone gets there. The alert is still showing as active in the property-manager portal, and I have not been able to clear it from my end. I would be very grateful if you could look at the sensor's status and tell me whether it is reporting a genuine wet reading, whether the battery or connection looks healthy, and whether there is anything you can do remotely in the meantime, since I would like to decide whether I need to drive over tonight or call someone out. Please let me know what you are able to see, and I can be reached at this email address or through the portal. Thank you so much for your help.

Kind regards,
Maya
Community Manager, Fernbrook Commons

scenario.premise: A leak sensor is alerting in a vacant unit and no one is on site to check it
